authorship: HALEX-AI staging draft, 2026-11-01. Summaries written in HALEX-AI's own words from general knowledge of these tools; no documentation text copied. Every entry links to the tool's official documentation. NOT a live page pack.
gate: Gates when each pack has >=10 entries, every entry linked to official docs, authorship label intact, no scraped content. Validator: library-pack-expansion-validate.py in this directory. Queue entry stays pending until Allen verifies the packs and promotes them himself.

entries.summary: Create a new repository in the current directory, or reinitialize an existing one so its working files become tracked.
entries.title: git init

entries.summary: Copy an existing repository, including its history, into a new local directory.
entries.title: git clone

entries.summary: Show which files changed, which are staged, and which are untracked, so you know the state of the working tree before committing.
entries.title: git status

entries.summary: Stage file changes so they are included in the next commit; staging lets you commit part of your work at a time.
entries.title: git add

entries.summary: Record the staged changes as a new commit with a message describing what changed and why.
entries.title: git commit

entries.summary: List past commits, newest first, with their messages and identifiers, so you can trace how the project reached its current state.
entries.title: git log

entries.summary: List, create, or delete branches, letting separate lines of work proceed without disturbing each other.
entries.title: git branch

entries.summary: Fold another branch's commits into the current branch, combining two lines of work into one history.
entries.title: git merge

entries.summary: Fetch new commits from a remote repository and merge them into the current branch, bringing local work up to date.
entries.title: git pull

entries.summary: Send local commits to a remote repository so others can fetch them and the work is backed up off your machine.
entries.title: git push

entries.summary: List the contents of a directory, with options to show hidden files, sizes, and one entry per line.
entries.title: ls — list directory contents

entries.summary: Change the shell's current directory; the Bourne-shell-builtins section of the Bash manual documents this builtin.
entries.title: cd — change directory

entries.summary: Print the full path of the current working directory, so you always know where you are in the filesystem.
entries.title: pwd — print working directory

entries.summary: Copy files or directories to a new location; the original stays where it was.
entries.title: cp — copy files

entries.summary: Move or rename files and directories; moving within one filesystem is a rename, not a copy.
entries.title: mv — move or rename

entries.summary: Remove files or directories; removals are not undoable, so recursive and forced removal need care.
entries.title: rm — remove files

entries.summary: Search file contents for lines matching a pattern, and print the matching lines.
entries.title: grep — search file contents

entries.summary: Walk a directory tree and list files matching tests such as name, type, or modification time.
entries.title: find — find files by test

entries.summary: Change the read, write, and execute permissions of files and directories for owner, group, and others.
entries.title: chmod — change permissions

entries.summary: Send a command's output to a file instead of the screen, or feed a file to a command as input, using the shell's redirection operators.
entries.title: Pipes and redirection

entries.summary: Read rows from one or more tables, choosing which columns to return and in what order.
entries.title: SELECT — read rows

entries.summary: Keep only the rows that satisfy a condition, filtering the result before it is returned.
entries.title: WHERE — filter rows

entries.summary: Combine rows from two tables where a shared value matches, so related records appear side by side.
entries.title: JOIN — combine tables

entries.summary: Collect rows that share a value into groups, so an aggregate such as a count or sum can be computed per group.
entries.title: GROUP BY — aggregate per group

entries.summary: Add new rows to a table, supplying a value for each column being written.
entries.title: INSERT — add rows

entries.summary: Change the values in existing rows that match a condition; without a condition every row changes.
entries.title: UPDATE — change rows

entries.summary: Remove rows that match a condition; without a condition every row is removed.
entries.title: DELETE — remove rows

entries.summary: Define a new table with named columns and their types, plus any constraints the data must satisfy.
entries.title: CREATE TABLE — define a table

entries.summary: Build an index on one or more columns so lookups and joins on those columns run faster, at the cost of slower writes.
entries.title: CREATE INDEX — speed up lookups

entries.summary: Wrap several statements in a transaction so they succeed together or roll back together, keeping the data consistent.
entries.title: Transactions — all or nothing

entries.summary: Compile and run a Go program, or build it into an executable file, from the module's source.
entries.title: go run / go build

entries.summary: Start a new module, which names the project and records the dependencies it uses.
entries.title: go mod init — start a module

entries.summary: Reformat Go source files to the standard layout, so code from different authors looks consistent.
entries.title: go fmt — standard formatting

entries.summary: Run a package's tests: small functions that check a piece of code behaves as expected.
entries.title: go test — run tests

entries.summary: Check code for suspicious constructs the compiler accepts but that are probably mistakes.
entries.title: go vet — catch mistakes

entries.summary: Organize code into packages, each a directory of source files that other packages import by path.
entries.title: Packages and imports

entries.summary: Run a function concurrently with the rest of the program by starting it as a lightweight goroutine.
entries.title: Goroutines — lightweight concurrency

entries.summary: Let goroutines pass values to each other through channels, so concurrent work can coordinate without shared memory.
entries.title: Channels — communicate between goroutines

entries.summary: Handle failures by returning an error value alongside the result, and checking it before using the result.
entries.title: Error handling — return errors as values

entries.summary: Show the documentation for a package, function, or type from the installed source, without opening a browser.
entries.title: go doc — read docs locally
